note: WAEC/NECO Mathematics Paper 1, round 2: geometry, mensuration, latitudes and longitudes, trigonometry, bearings, statistics, probability and introductory calculus (WASSCE-standard applied objective items; answers machine-verified).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two angles of a triangle are 47° and 68°. Find the third angle.
questions.explanation: Angles of a triangle add to 180°: 180 − 47 − 68 = 65 degrees.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find each interior angle of a regular pentagon.
questions.explanation: Each interior angle = (5 − 2) × 180 ÷ 5 = 108 degrees.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find each exterior angle of a regular octagon.
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 degrees.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. Find x.
questions.explanation: The angles add to 360°, so 10x = 360 and x = 36.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a right-angled triangle the two acute angles are 2y and 3y + 10. Find y.
questions.explanation: The acute angles add to 90°: 5y + 10 = 90, so y = 16.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One co-interior angle is 118°. Find the other.
questions.explanation: Co-interior (allied) angles between parallel lines add to 180°: 180 − 118 = 62.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1,440°. How many sides has the polygon?
questions.explanation: n sides give (n − 2) × 180 = 1440, so n − 2 = 8 and n = 10.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: One of the equal angles of an isosceles triangle is 40°. Find the vertex angle.
questions.explanation: The two equal angles total 80°, so the vertex angle is 180 − 80 = 100 degrees.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest angle.
questions.explanation: Nine parts make 180°, so each part is 20° and the largest is 4 × 20 = 80 degrees.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the sum of the interior angles of a regular polygon with 12 sides.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Triangles ABC and PQR are similar. AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and PQ = 10 cm. Find QR.
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, so QR = 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 8 cm and 15 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras: √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An arc subtends an angle of 130° at the centre of a circle. Find the angle it subtends at the circumference.
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference: 130 ÷ 2 = 65.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A chord of a circle is 16 cm long and lies 6 cm from the centre. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.explanation: Half the chord is 8 cm; radius = √(8² + 6²) = √100 = 10 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A, B and C lie on a circle with AB as a diameter. Find angle ACB.
questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral, one angle is 71°. Find its opposite angle.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: 180 − 71 = 109.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A tangent to a circle is 12 cm long, drawn from a point 13 cm from the centre. Find the radius.
questions.explanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius: r = √(13² − 12²) = √25 = 5 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The radius of a circle is 15 cm. Find the length of a chord that is 9 cm from the centre.
questions.explanation: Half the chord = √(225 − 81) = 12, so the chord is 24 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An arc subtends 72° at the centre of a circle of radius 35 cm. Find the length of the arc (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 14 cm (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 12 cm and 18 cm and whose height is 8 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the circumference of a circle of diameter 21 cm (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the volume of a cone of base radius 6 cm and vertical height 7 cm (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm, correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the total surface area of a cube of edge 5 cm.
questions.explanation: Six faces of 25 cm² each give 150 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rectangular tank is 3 m long, 2 m wide and 1.5 m high. Find its capacity in litres (1 m³ = 1,000 litres).
questions.explanation: Volume = 9 m³ = 9,000 litres.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the area of a sector of radius 10.5 cm and angle 120° (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of a rectangle is 84 cm² and its width is 7 cm. Find its perimeter.
questions.explanation: Length = 12 cm, so the perimeter = 2 × (12 + 7) = 38 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the total surface area of a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 14 cm (take π = 22/7).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A square has an area of 196 cm². Find its perimeter.
questions.explanation: The side is 14 cm, so the perimeter is 4 × 14 = 56 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the length of the diagonal of a rectangle measuring 9 cm by 12 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The volume of a cuboid is 720 cm³ and its base measures 12 cm by 5 cm. Find its height.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm (take π = 22/7).
questions.explanation: Curved surface 2πr² plus flat face πr² gives 3πr² = 462 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the perimeter of a semicircle of diameter 14 cm (take π = 22/7).
questions.explanation: Half the circumference is 22 cm, plus the diameter 14 cm, giving 36 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Taking the earth as a sphere of radius 6,370 km, find the radius of the parallel of latitude 60°N.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the distance, measured along their meridian, between A(50°N, 20°E) and B(20°N, 20°E), taking R = 6,300 km and π = 22/7.
questions.explanation: The latitude difference is 30°, so distance = (30/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 6,300 = 3,300 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the distance along the equator between P(0°, 10°E) and Q(0°, 50°E), taking R = 6,300 km and π = 22/7.
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 40°, so distance = (40/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 6,300 = 4,400 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: On which parallel of latitude is the radius of the circle half the radius of the earth?
questions.explanation: We need cos θ = 0.5, and cos 60° = 0.5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find, to the nearest kilometre, the radius of the parallel of latitude 45°N, taking R = 6,370 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two towns both lie on the parallel 60°N and differ in longitude by 30°. Find their distance apart along the parallel (R = 6,300 km, π = 22/7).
questions.explanation: Radius of the parallel = 3,150 km, so distance = (30/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 3,150 = 1,650 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Evaluate 2 sin 30° + 3 cos 60°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If cos θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find sin θ.
questions.explanation: sin θ = √(1 − 9/25) = 4/5, using the 3-4-5 triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If sin θ = 5/13 and θ is acute, find cos θ.
questions.explanation: cos θ = √(1 − 25/169) = 12/13, using the 5-12-13 triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solve 2 sin θ = 1 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°.
questions.explanation: sin θ = 0.5, and the angle whose sine is 0.5 is 30°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solve cos θ = −½ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°.
questions.explanation: cos 60° = 0.5, so in the second quadrant θ = 180 − 60 = 120°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If tan θ = 3/4 and 0° < θ < 90°, find sin θ.
questions.explanation: The ratio 3 : 4 gives hypotenuse 5, so sin θ = 3/5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In which quadrant does θ lie if sin θ < 0 and cos θ > 0?
questions.explanation: Cosine is positive in the first and fourth quadrants, but sine is negative only in the fourth.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a right-angled triangle the side opposite an angle θ is 8 cm and the side adjacent is 6 cm. Find θ to the nearest degree.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If θ is acute and sin θ = cos 40°, find θ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Simplify sin²θ + cos²θ.
questions.explanation: This is the Pythagorean identity, true for every angle θ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the height of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm, in surd form.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Evaluate sec 45°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 60 m from its foot is 30°. Find the height of the tower, correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the top of a cliff 100 m above sea level, the angle of depression of a boat is 45°. Find the horizontal distance of the boat from the foot of the cliff.
questions.explanation: Distance = 100 ÷ tan 45° = 100 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A ladder 13 m long leans against a wall, making an angle of 60° with the ground. Find how far up the wall it reaches, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: Height = 13 sin 60° ≈ 11.3 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the top of a tower 45 m tall, the angles of depression of two cars C and D on the same side of the tower are 30° and 60°. Find the distance CD, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: Distances from the foot: 45/tan30 ≈ 77.9 m and 45/tan60 ≈ 26.0 m, so CD ≈ 52.0 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A vertical stick 2 m long casts a shadow when the angle of elevation of the sun is 30°. Find the length of the shadow, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Shadow = 2 ÷ tan 30° ≈ 3.46 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A boy 1.7 m tall stands 20 m from a building. The angle of elevation of the top of the building from his head is 45°. Find the height of the building.
questions.explanation: The building is 20 tan 45° = 20 m above his head, so it is 21.7 m tall.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An aircraft flying at 300 m has an angle of depression of 60° to a point on the ground. Find its horizontal distance from the point, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: Distance = 300 ÷ tan 60° ≈ 173.2 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From a window 15 m above the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a nearby building 30 m tall is 30°. Find the horizontal distance between the window and the building, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: The height difference is 15 m, so distance = 15 ÷ tan 30° ≈ 26.0 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A man walks 3 km due east and then 4 km due north. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: The path forms a 3-4-5 right triangle, so he is 5 km away.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The bearing of P from Q is 065°. Find the bearing of Q from P.
questions.explanation: A back bearing differs by 180°: 065° + 180° = 245°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The bearing of X from Y is 270°. Find the bearing of Y from X.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A hunter walks 5 km due south and then 12 km due east. Find his bearing from his starting point, to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: tan of the angle east of south = 12/5, giving 67°, so the bearing is 180 − 67 = 113°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A plane flies 100 km from airport A on a bearing of 045°. How far east of A is it, correct to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: Eastward distance = 100 sin 45° ≈ 70.7 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A ship sails 150 km from P on a bearing of 240°. How far south of P is it then?
questions.explanation: 240° is 60° past south on the westerly side: south distance = 150 cos 60° = 75 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A boat sails 30 km due east and then 40 km due south. How far is it from its starting point?
questions.explanation: The legs form a 30-40-50 right triangle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An aircraft flies 60 km due west and then 80 km due north. How far is it from where it started?
questions.explanation: The displacement is √(60² + 80²) = 100 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the mean of 4, 7, 9, 12 and 18.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the median of 3, 8, 5, 11, 7, 2 and 9.
questions.explanation: Arranged in order: 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11 — the middle value is 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the mode of 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 4, 6 and 7.
questions.explanation: The value 4 appears three times, more than any other.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the range of 15, 22, 8, 31 and 19.
questions.explanation: Range = largest − smallest = 31 − 8 = 23.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a test, 4 pupils scored 6 marks each and 6 pupils scored 8 marks each. Find the mean mark.
questions.explanation: Total = 24 + 48 = 72, shared by 10 pupils: 7.2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean of five numbers is 12. Four of them are 10, 11, 13 and 14. Find the fifth number.
questions.explanation: The total is 60, and 60 − 48 = 12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the median of the numbers 4, 6, 9 and 11?
questions.explanation: With an even count, average the two middle values: (6 + 9)/2 = 7.5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a pie chart representing 120 students, a sector has an angle of 90°. How many students does the sector represent?
questions.explanation: The sector is a quarter of the chart: 90/360 × 120 = 30 students.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean of 3, 5, x, 9 and 11 is 7. Find x.
questions.explanation: The total is 35, and 35 − 28 = 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean age of 20 boys is 15 years and the mean age of 30 girls is 12 years. Find the mean age of the whole class.
questions.explanation: Total ages = 300 + 360 = 660, shared by 50 pupils: 13.2 years.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The heights, in cm, of 8 boys are 150, 152, 154, 155, 157, 158, 160 and 165. Find the median height.
questions.explanation: The two middle values are 155 and 157, so the median is 156 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The marks 2, 3, 5 and 7 have frequencies 3, 2, 4 and 1 respectively. Find the mean mark.
questions.explanation: Total = 6 + 6 + 20 + 7 = 39 over 10 items, so the mean is 3.9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Calculate the mean of the first ten positive integers.
questions.explanation: The integers 1 to 10 add up to 55, so the mean is 5.5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the interquartile range of 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 15.
questions.explanation: The lower quartile is the 2nd value (5) and the upper quartile is the 6th (12), so the IQR is 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
questions.explanation: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5: three outcomes out of six.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A fair coin is tossed twice. Find the probability of getting two heads.
questions.explanation: The four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT; only one is HH.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is red.
questions.explanation: There are 10 balls in all, so P(red) = 4/10 = 2/5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A box contains 5 white, 3 green and 2 yellow balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is not white.
questions.explanation: Not-white balls are 3 + 2 = 5 out of 10.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the sum of the scores is 7.
questions.explanation: Six of the 36 outcomes add to 7, so P = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A letter is chosen at random from the word EXAMINATION. Find the probability that it is a vowel.
questions.explanation: The word has 11 letters of which 6 are vowels (E, A, I, A, I, O).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a class of 40 students, 25 like Mathematics. If a student is chosen at random, find the probability that the student likes Mathematics.
questions.explanation: Twenty-five of the forty students like Maths, so P = 25/40 = 5/8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 20. Find the probability that it is divisible by 4.
questions.explanation: The multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20: five out of twenty.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The probability that it rains on a given day is 0.3. Find the probability that it does not rain.
questions.explanation: The two probabilities must add to 1, so P(no rain) = 1 − 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains 3 red and 5 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability that both are red.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Given y = x³, find dy/dx when x = 2.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x², so at x = 2 it is 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Given y = 4x³ − 2x, find dy/dx when x = 1.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 12x² − 2, so at x = 1 it is 12 − 2 = 10.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the gradient of the curve y = x² − 4x at the point where x = 5.
questions.explanation: The gradient is dy/dx = 2x − 4, so at x = 5 it is 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the maximum value of y = 10 − 2x − x².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The velocity of a particle is v = 3t² − 12t. Find its acceleration when t = 2.
questions.explanation: Acceleration = dv/dt = 6t − 12, so at t = 2 it is 0 m/s².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Given y = (2x + 1)², find dy/dx when x = 2.
questions.explanation: By the chain rule dy/dx = 4(2x + 1), so at x = 2 it is 4 × 5 = 20.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The radius of a circle increases at 0.5 cm/s. Find the rate at which the area is increasing when r = 7 cm (take π = 22/7).
